newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London creep up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London creep up in thin trade.

text.p: Hong Kong shares traded in London crept higher in thin trade on Tuesday, drawing inspiration from London and New York stock markets, dealers said.

The Hang Seng London Reference index advanced 11.02 points to close at 11,223.62, after reaching a high of 11,334.40 earlier in the session. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng index also closed 11.02 points higher at 11,223.62.

Brokers said shares edged higher in morning trade largely on the back of strength in HSBC Holdings, which drew support from the London stock exchange. But shares lost their earlier enthusiasm during the afternoon as Wall Street opened lower.
"The market initially was quite firm, but this afternoon in line with the slightly softer opening on Wall Street and a little weakness in the U.S. bond market, prices have softened," said one trader.
By 1530 GMT, the Dow Jones industrial index stood 16.65 points down at 5,717.19.
Brokers said attention was now turning toward U.S. PPI and CPI data due out on Friday.
